request_asylum_subtitle: How do asylum applications, initial reception, registration and interviews work?
asylum_rights_subtitle: Which one do you have to do?What are you allowed to do?

entity1.id1.title: Asylum application in Austria
entity1.id1.subtitle: How do you apply for asylum in Austria?
entity1.id1.entry1.title: Can I apply for asylum abroad?
entity1.id1.entry1.subtitle: No, an asylum application can only be submitted personally and verbally within the country (i.e. Austria).It is therefore not possible to apply for asylum in Austria from abroad!
entity1.id1.entry2.title: Where can I apply for asylum?
entity1.id1.entry2.subtitle: You can submit an asylum application to any police authority or police officer.
entity1.id1.entry3.title: When does asylum apply?
entity1.id1.entry3.subtitle:
The prerequisite for applying for asylum is a well-founded fear of persecution for certain reasons for fleeing:
•Breed
•Religion
•Nationality
•Belonging to a particular social group
•or because of their political beliefs.
entity1.id1.entry4.title: What's next?
entity1.id1.entry4.subtitle: The asylum seeker is taken to an initial reception center (e.g. Traiskirchen or Thalham).A procedure card (“green card” in accordance with Section 50 Asylum Act) will be issued for them.
entity1.id2.title: Initial reception and registration
entity1.id2.subtitle: What happens after you apply for asylum?
entity1.id2.entry1.title: interview
entity1.id2.entry1.subtitle: The application is registered and an initial survey with interpreting support is carried out.
entity1.id2.entry2.title: search
entity1.id2.entry2.subtitle: The police officers take the personal details, search the luggage, check the documents presented and take fingerprints.
entity1.id2.entry3.title: State all reasons for escape
entity1.id2.entry3.subtitle: It is important to state as many reasons as possible when submitting your application.
entity1.id3.title: Admission process
entity1.id3.subtitle: What is checked during the asylum procedure?
entity1.id3.entry1.title: Austria is responsible
entity1.id3.entry1.subtitle: The admission process clarifies whether Austria is responsible for the content of the asylum procedure and whether the application is admissible.
entity1.id3.entry2.title: If Austria is not responsible:
entity1.id3.entry2.subtitle:
•if the asylum seeker has already applied for asylum in another Dublin country (EU, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland) or
•has already received a residence permit there.
•if another Dublin state has permitted or not prevented legal (visa) or illegal entry (sea or green border).
entity1.id3.entry3.title: Stay
entity1.id3.entry3.subtitle:
During the admission process, you are only permitted to stay in the district of the respective care center.
The area restriction to the respective district is noted on the green process map.
entity1.id3.entry4.title: Interview at the Federal Office for Immigration and Asylum (BFA):
entity1.id3.entry4.subtitle:
•This interview is an interrogation lasting several hours.
•Asylum seekers are asked about their personal circumstances, their journey to Austria and the reasons for their flight.
•In this interview, it is important to make the “legitimate fear of persecution” credible (Art. 1 GRC).
•The interview will be conducted in an understandable language and translated by an interpreter.
•Asylum seekers may be accompanied by legal representation.A person you trust can also come along, but they must remain silent.
•The transcript of the interview will be re-translated at the end.It is important to correct statements that were not recorded correctly.
entity1.id4.title: Content procedures
entity1.id4.subtitle: What's next?
entity1.id4.entry1.title: White card
entity1.id4.entry1.subtitle: If the procedure has been approved, the asylum seeker receives the “white card” (residence authorization card in accordance with Section 51 AsylG).This documents a right of residence throughout the entire asylum procedure.
entity1.id4.entry2.title: Where are you allowed to stay?
entity1.id4.entry2.subtitle: Asylum seekers are allowed to move throughout the entire federal territory (i.e. Austria), but can only live in the federal state assigned to them.
entity1.id4.entry3.title: Basic care quarters
entity1.id4.entry3.subtitle: During the process, asylum seekers live in basic accommodation.
entity1.id5.title: Asylum decision
entity1.id5.subtitle: Important information about the asylum decision
entity1.id5.entry1.title: Who decides on the asylum application?
entity1.id5.entry1.subtitle: The BFA decides on the asylum application by means of a decision.
entity1.id5.entry2.title: How long does an asylum procedure take?
entity1.id5.entry2.subtitle: The BFA must issue a decision within six months.
entity1.id5.entry3.title: How do I get the asylum decision?
entity1.id5.entry3.subtitle: The decision is sent to the asylum seeker or the legal representative.
entity1.id5.entry4.title: What to do if you receive a negative decision
entity1.id5.entry4.subtitle: The essential components of the decision are the result of the procedure (ruling) and the options for making a complaint (information on legal remedies).
entity1.id6.title: Complaint
entity1.id6.subtitle: What can you do about a negative asylum application?
entity1.id6.entry1.title: You can file a complaint
entity1.id6.entry1.subtitle: An appeal can be lodged against the BFA's decisions with the Federal Administrative Court.
entity1.id6.entry2.title: What's happening there?
entity1.id6.entry2.subtitle: There, independent judges will decide on the application again.
entity1.id6.entry3.title: Legal advisor
entity1.id6.entry3.subtitle: If a complaint is made, a legal advisor is usually provided free of charge.Representation by a lawyer is also possible at your own expense.
entity1.id6.entry4.title: Deadlines and formalities
entity1.id6.entry4.subtitle: The complaint must be submitted in writing and in a timely manner.The complaint to the Federal Administrative Court must be submitted to the Federal Office for Immigration and Asylum (BFA).This submits the complaint to the Federal Administrative Court.The appeal period begins from the delivery of the notice and is normally 4 weeks.
entity2.id1.title: Asylum application in Austria
entity2.id1.subtitle: Basic information about applying for asylum
entity2.id1.entry1.title: Can I apply for asylum abroad?
entity2.id1.entry1.subtitle: No, an asylum application can only be submitted in person on Austrian territory.There is no way to apply for asylum from another country.
entity2.id1.entry2.title: Where can I apply for asylum?
entity2.id1.entry2.subtitle: Asylum can be applied for at any police station, at the Federal Office for Immigration and Asylum (BFA) or at the border from border officials.
entity2.id1.entry3.title: Requirements for asylum
entity2.id1.entry3.subtitle:
Asylum can be applied for if there is a well-founded fear of persecution due to:
• Race
• Religion
• Nationality
• Belonging to a particular social group
• Political beliefs
exists.
entity2.id1.entry4.title: First steps after submitting your application
entity2.id1.entry4.subtitle: After submitting your application, you will be taken to the initial reception center and given a procedure card (“green card”).
entity2.id2.title: Initial reception and registration
entity2.id2.subtitle: What happens in the first few days after submitting the application
entity2.id2.entry1.title: Initial survey
entity2.id2.entry1.subtitle: An initial survey with interpreter support is carried out to record personal data and reasons for fleeing.
entity2.id2.entry2.title: Biometric data capture
entity2.id2.entry2.subtitle: Fingerprints are taken and photos are taken.This data is stored in the EURODAC system.
entity2.id2.entry3.title: Medical examination
entity2.id2.entry3.subtitle: A basic medical examination is carried out to rule out infectious diseases.
entity2.id2.entry4.subtitle: You will be accommodated in an initial reception center (such as Traiskirchen) until your case is processed further.
entity2.id3.title: Admission process
entity2.id3.subtitle: Examination of Austria's jurisdiction
entity2.id3.entry1.title: Dublin procedure
entity2.id3.entry1.subtitle: It will be checked whether Austria is responsible for your asylum procedure according to the Dublin III Regulation.
entity2.id3.entry2.title: Reasons for exclusion
entity2.id3.entry2.subtitle:
Austria is not responsible if:
• You have already applied for asylum in another Dublin country
• You have a residence permit in another Dublin country
• You arrived from a safe third country
entity2.id3.entry3.title: Residence restrictions
entity2.id3.entry3.subtitle: During the admission process, you are only allowed to stay in the district of your care center.
entity2.id3.entry4.title: Issue of the procedure card
entity2.id3.entry4.subtitle: You will receive a green procedure card that documents your temporary right of residence.
entity2.id4.title: Content procedure
entity2.id4.subtitle: Checking your reasons for asylum
entity2.id4.entry1.title: Main procedure
entity2.id4.entry1.subtitle: After positive admission, the substantive process to examine your reasons for asylum begins.
entity2.id4.entry2.title: White card
entity2.id4.entry2.subtitle: You will receive a white residence permit card that is valid throughout the entire procedure.
entity2.id4.entry3.title: Personal hearing
entity2.id4.entry3.subtitle: A detailed hearing will be held at the BFA, during which your reasons for fleeing will be discussed in detail.
entity2.id4.entry4.title: Legal representation
entity2.id4.entry4.subtitle: You have the right to free legal advice and can be accompanied by someone you trust.
entity2.id5.title: Asylum decision
entity2.id5.subtitle: The decision on your application
entity2.id5.entry1.title: Decision deadline
entity2.id5.entry1.subtitle: The BFA must decide on your application within 6 months.In complex cases, this period may be extended.
entity2.id5.entry2.title: Positive decision
entity2.id5.entry2.subtitle: If you are recognized as a person entitled to asylum, you will receive an asylum decision and a residence permit.
entity2.id5.entry3.title: Negative decision
entity2.id5.entry3.subtitle: If you are rejected, you will receive a negative decision with instructions on how to appeal.
entity2.id5.entry4.title: Subsidiary protection
entity2.id5.entry4.subtitle: If asylum is not granted, subsidiary protection may be considered if you are at risk of serious harm in your home country.
entity2.id6.title: Legal remedies
entity2.id6.subtitle: What to do if rejected?
entity2.id6.entry1.title: lodge a complaint
entity2.id6.entry1.subtitle: You can lodge a complaint against a negative decision with the Federal Administrative Court within 4 weeks.
entity2.id6.entry2.title: Free legal advice
entity2.id6.entry2.subtitle: A legal advisor is available to you free of charge to file a complaint.
entity2.id6.entry3.title: Right of residence during appeal
entity2.id6.entry3.subtitle: As long as your complaint is ongoing, you can stay in Austria.
entity2.id6.entry4.title: Further remedies
entity2.id6.entry4.subtitle: You can appeal the decision of the Federal Administrative Court to the Administrative Court or lodge a constitutional complaint.
entity2.id6.entry5.title: Exhaustion of legal remedies
entity2.id6.entry5.subtitle: Deportation can only take place after all legal remedies have been exhausted.
entity2.id7.title: After a positive decision
entity2.id7.subtitle: Integration and residence
entity2.id7.entry1.title: Residence permit
entity2.id7.entry1.subtitle: You will receive a residence permit that is initially valid for 3 years and can be extended.
entity2.id7.entry2.title: Labor market access
entity2.id7.entry2.subtitle: As a recognized refugee, you have unrestricted access to the labor market.
entity2.id7.entry3.title: Family reunification
entity2.id7.entry3.subtitle: Under certain conditions you can bring family members to Austria.
entity2.id7.entry4.title: Integration measures
entity2.id7.entry4.subtitle: You are entitled to German courses and integration measures.
entity2.id8.title: Rights & Responsibilities
entity2.id8.subtitle: What you can and must do
entity2.id8.entry1.title: Basic care
entity2.id8.entry1.subtitle: You are entitled to accommodation, food, medical care and pocket money.
entity2.id8.entry2.title: Obligation to cooperate
entity2.id8.entry2.subtitle: You must cooperate in all official procedures and provide truthful information.
entity2.id8.entry3.title: Reporting requirement
entity2.id8.entry3.subtitle: You must report address changes to the relevant authority.
entity2.id8.entry4.title: Residence requirement
entity2.id8.entry4.subtitle: You must reside in your assigned state.
entity3.id1.title: General rights and obligations
entity3.id1.subtitle: Basic rules for asylum seekers in Austria
entity3.id1.entry1.title: Duty to tell the truth
entity3.id1.entry1.subtitle: You must provide truthful and complete information about your request.False information can have a negative impact on the asylum application.
entity3.id1.entry2.title: present evidence
entity3.id1.entry2.subtitle: Submit any evidence you have as quickly as possible.This strengthens your credibility.
entity3.id1.entry3.title: Identity verification
entity3.id1.entry3.subtitle: Participate in the identification process (fingerprints, photographs).This is required by law.
entity3.id1.entry4.title: Carry procedure card
entity3.id1.entry4.subtitle: You will receive a procedure card.Always carry these with you!It serves as an identification document.
entity3.id2.title: The procedure cards
entity3.id2.subtitle: Meaning of the different cards
entity3.id2.entry1.title: Green card
entity3.id2.entry1.subtitle: Means that the approval process begins.You are not allowed to leave your assigned district.
entity3.id2.entry2.title: White card
entity3.id2.entry2.subtitle: Means that the asylum procedure is carried out in Austria.You are now allowed to leave the district, but not the state.
entity3.id2.entry3.title: Obey laws
entity3.id2.entry3.subtitle: You must follow the laws of Austria.This applies to everyone in the country.
entity3.id2.entry4.title: Medical care
entity3.id2.entry4.subtitle: You receive medical care like Austrian citizens.This is a fundamental right.
entity3.id3.title: Finance & Property
entity3.id3.subtitle: Rules regarding money and personal items
entity3.id3.entry1.title: Cash withdrawal
entity3.id3.entry1.subtitle: When applying for asylum, the authorities are allowed to take cash (over €120) brought with you up to a maximum of €840 in order to cover accommodation costs.
entity3.id3.entry2.title: refund
entity3.id3.entry2.subtitle: If more cash was taken from you than needed, you are entitled to a refund of the remaining amount.
entity3.id3.entry3.title: Disk
entity3.id3.entry3.subtitle: The authority is allowed to evaluate data carriers (cell phones) to establish identity.These must then be returned.
entity3.id3.entry4.title: Data protection
entity3.id3.entry4.subtitle: The data evaluation only serves to establish identity.Personal data is subject to data protection.
entity3.id4.title: Dates and procedures
entity3.id4.subtitle: Important duties in the process
entity3.id4.entry1.title: Interview appointments
entity3.id4.entry1.subtitle: Arrive on time for all interview appointments.Failure to do so can have negative consequences.
entity3.id4.entry2.title: Sick note
entity3.id4.entry2.subtitle: If you are ill, please deregister immediately and provide a medical confirmation.
entity3.id4.entry3.title: Procedural consequences
entity3.id4.entry3.subtitle: Failure to appear can lead to the discontinuation of proceedings, a negative decision or an order for arrest.
entity3.id4.entry4.title: House rules
entity3.id4.entry4.subtitle: The BFA house rules apply in federal care facilities.Follow these rules.
entity3.id5.title: Stay & Accommodation
entity3.id5.subtitle: Rules for living and movement
entity3.id5.entry1.title: supply
entity3.id5.entry1.subtitle: They receive three meals a day, hygiene products, clothing and monthly pocket money.
entity3.id5.entry2.title: Report absence
entity3.id5.entry2.subtitle: Report absences of more than 48 hours to your accommodation provider.
entity3.id5.entry3.title: Delivery address
entity3.id5.entry3.subtitle: You must report any change to your delivery address to the authorities immediately.
entity3.id5.entry4.title: Authorized delivery agent
entity3.id5.entry4.subtitle: You can name an authorized delivery agent (acquaintance, organization) to receive your mail.
entity3.id6.title: Education & Language
entity3.id6.subtitle: School, kindergarten and German courses
entity3.id6.entry1.title: Compulsory schooling
entity3.id6.entry1.subtitle: All children aged 6-15 must go to school in Austria.This also applies to refugee children.
entity3.id6.entry2.title: Kindergarten requirement
entity3.id6.entry2.subtitle: Children aged 5-6 must complete a compulsory year of kindergarten.
entity3.id6.entry3.title: Legal consequences
entity3.id6.entry3.subtitle: If you violate your school or kindergarten requirement, there are legal consequences and penalties.
entity3.id6.entry4.title: learn German
entity3.id6.entry4.subtitle: German is important for everyday life, work and offices.Take advantage of free learning opportunities.
entity3.id7.title: Work and employment
entity3.id7.subtitle: Rules for starting work
entity3.id7.entry1.title: Employment permit
entity3.id7.entry1.subtitle: For regular work you need an employment permit.The AMS examines the labor market.
entity3.id7.entry2.title: Household activities
entity3.id7.entry2.subtitle: Asylum seekers after 3 months are allowed to work in private households (service check).
entity3.id7.entry3.title: Auxiliary work
entity3.id7.entry3.subtitle: Approved asylum seekers can carry out unskilled work in accommodation or charitable work.
entity3.id7.entry4.title: Labor market test
entity3.id7.entry4.subtitle: Before approval, the AMS checks whether Austrian employees are available.
entity3.id8.title: Obligation to report and stay
entity3.id8.subtitle: Residence and movement
entity3.id8.entry1.title: Change of address
entity3.id8.entry1.subtitle: Report any change in your residential address to the registration authority within 3 days.
entity3.id8.entry2.title: Change of state
entity3.id8.entry2.subtitle: You are not allowed to move your residence to another federal state without permission.
entity3.id8.entry3.title: Leave Austria
entity3.id8.entry3.subtitle: If you leave Austria, your asylum procedure will be stopped!
entity3.id8.entry4.title: Registration authority
entity3.id8.entry4.subtitle: In Austria, it is sufficient to register with the local registration authority within three days.
entity4.id1.title: Positive decision - asylum recognition
entity4.id1.subtitle: What does recognition as a person entitled to asylum mean?
entity4.id1.entry1.title: Residence permit
entity4.id1.entry1.subtitle: You will receive a 3-year residence permit as a person entitled to asylum.This can be extended after 3 years if the requirements still exist.
entity4.id1.entry2.title: Personal delivery
entity4.id1.entry2.subtitle: The positive decision will be delivered to you personally or by registered letter.Check all information carefully.
entity4.id1.entry3.title: Travel document
entity4.id1.entry3.subtitle: Those entitled to asylum can apply for a travel document for refugees.This enables travel to many countries (except the country of origin).
entity4.id1.entry4.title: Immediate rights
entity4.id1.entry4.subtitle: With the positive decision you will immediately receive: unrestricted access to the labor market, entitlement to family allowance and full social rights.
entity4.id2.title: First steps after recognition
entity4.id2.subtitle: What do you have to do after a positive decision?
entity4.id2.entry1.title: Apply for confirmation of registration
entity4.id2.entry1.subtitle: Apply to the registration authority for a registration confirmation with your new status within 2 weeks.
entity4.id2.entry2.title: social security
entity4.id2.entry2.subtitle: Register with the social insurance (ÖGK).You will receive an e-card for medical services.
entity4.id2.entry3.title: Labor market
entity4.id2.entry3.subtitle: You no longer need a work permit.You can take up any legal work.Register with the AMS for assistance.
entity4.id2.entry4.title: End basic care
entity4.id2.entry4.subtitle: Inform your care facility of the positive decision.Basic care ends 4 weeks after receipt of the notice.
entity4.id3.title: Integration & language courses
entity4.id3.subtitle: Obligations and offers after recognition
entity4.id3.entry1.title: Integration agreement
entity4.id3.entry1.subtitle: You must demonstrate German language skills at A2 level within 2 years and complete a values ​​and orientation course.
entity4.id3.entry2.title: German courses (ÖIF)
entity4.id3.entry2.subtitle: Free German courses at the Austrian Integration Fund.A1 and A2 courses are mandatory for extending your residence permit.
entity4.id3.entry3.title: Values ​​and orientation course
entity4.id3.entry3.subtitle: Compulsory course on Austrian values, history and the rule of law.Duration: 8 hours, free at the ÖIF.
entity4.id3.entry4.title: Pay attention to deadlines
entity4.id3.entry4.subtitle: The integration agreement must be fulfilled within 2 years.Otherwise, the extension of the residence permit may be refused.
entity4.id4.title: Family reunification
entity4.id4.subtitle: Bring family to Austria
entity4.id4.entry1.title: Authorized persons
entity4.id4.entry1.subtitle: Spouses, registered partners and minor children can be brought along.Parents and other relatives only in cases of hardship.
entity4.id4.entry2.title: Deadlines
entity4.id4.entry2.subtitle: Submit an application within 12 months of asylum recognition.After that, stricter requirements apply.
entity4.id4.entry3.title: Requirements
entity4.id4.entry3.subtitle: Sufficient living space, secure livelihood, health insurance for all family members.
entity4.id4.entry4.title: Proceedings
entity4.id4.entry4.subtitle: Submit an application to the Austrian consulate in the country of origin.Duration of the procedure: 6-12 months.
entity4.id5.title: Negative decision - rejection
entity4.id5.subtitle: What does the rejection of the asylum application mean?
entity4.id5.entry1.title: Check notification
entity4.id5.entry1.subtitle: Check the decision carefully: reasons for rejection, information on legal remedies and deadlines.Have a legal advisor explain it to you.
entity4.id5.entry2.title: Deadline for appeal
entity4.id5.entry2.subtitle: You have 4 weeks from delivery of the decision to lodge a complaint with the Federal Administrative Court.
entity4.id5.entry3.title: Stay during complaint
entity4.id5.entry3.subtitle: You are allowed to stay in Austria during the complaint period and the complaint procedure (suspending effect).
entity4.id5.entry4.title: Dublin repatriation
entity4.id5.entry4.subtitle: If Dublin is rejected: Austria is not responsible.They will be returned to the responsible EU country.Deadline: 6 months.
entity4.id6.title: Complaints Procedure
entity4.id6.subtitle: How do you file a complaint?
entity4.id6.entry1.title: Formal requirements
entity4.id6.entry1.subtitle: Complaints must be submitted in writing to the authority that issued the decision (BFA).Justification is required.
entity4.id6.entry2.title: Free legal advice
entity4.id6.entry2.subtitle: A legal advisor is available to help you with your complaint free of charge.Contact BBU, Caritas or Diakonie.
entity4.id6.entry3.title: New evidence
entity4.id6.entry3.subtitle: New evidence may be presented in the appeal process that was not available in the first proceeding.
entity4.id6.entry4.title: Duration of the procedure
entity4.id6.entry4.subtitle: The complaint process takes an average of 6-12 months.In urgent cases, an urgent application can be submitted.
entity4.id7.title: Subsidiary protection
entity4.id7.subtitle: Alternative if asylum is rejected
entity4.id7.entry1.title: Requirements
entity4.id7.entry1.subtitle: Subsidiary protection is granted when there is a threat of serious harm: death penalty, torture, inhumane treatment or serious individual threat of armed conflict.
entity4.id7.entry2.title: right
entity4.id7.entry2.subtitle: 1-year residence permit (extendable), work permit, access to social benefits, but limited family reunification.
entity4.id7.entry3.title: Automatic checking
entity4.id7.entry3.subtitle: The BFA automatically checks subsidiary protection if asylum is rejected.You do not need to submit a separate application.
entity4.id7.entry4.title: Proceedings
entity4.id7.entry4.subtitle: If subsidiary protection is granted, you will receive a separate decision.There is also a right to lodge a complaint.
entity4.id8.title: Deportation and return
entity4.id8.subtitle: What happens if I am finally rejected?
entity4.id8.entry1.title: Departure deadline
entity4.id8.entry1.subtitle: After final rejection: 1 month period to leave the country.If you leave the country voluntarily: support from the REAG/GARP program.
entity4.id8.entry2.title: Return advice
entity4.id8.entry2.subtitle: Free advice from IOM or Caritas about return options, financial support and reintegration.
entity4.id8.entry3.title: Voluntary return
entity4.id8.entry3.subtitle: Voluntary return is financially supported: flight ticket, travel money (up to €1000), reintegration assistance in the home country.
entity4.id8.entry4.title: Forced detention & deportation
entity4.id8.entry4.subtitle: In case of non-voluntary departure: detention pending deportation (max. 10 months) possible, followed by deportation under police escort.
entity4.id9.title: Humanitarian right to remain
entity4.id9.subtitle: Exceptions in the event of obstacles to deportation
entity4.id9.entry1.title: Illness
entity4.id9.entry1.subtitle: Serious illness that cannot be treated in the home country can justify a humanitarian right to remain.
entity4.id9.entry2.title: Family life
entity4.id9.entry2.subtitle: Close ties to family members living in Austria (especially children) can justify the right to remain.
entity4.id9.entry3.title: integration
entity4.id9.entry3.subtitle: After a long stay (several years) and good integration, the right to remain can be granted for humanitarian reasons.
entity4.id9.entry4.title: Application
entity4.id9.entry4.subtitle: Humanitarian right to remain must be applied for separately at the BFA.Success rate is low, legal advice is essential.
entity4.id10.title: Important addresses & help
entity4.id10.subtitle: Who can help?
entity4.id10.entry1.title: Legal advice
entity4.id10.entry1.subtitle: BBU, Caritas, Diakonie, Asylkoordination offer free legal advice for complaints and further steps.
entity4.id10.entry2.title: Return assistance
entity4.id10.entry2.subtitle: IOM (International Organization for Migration): +43 1 585 33 22, info@iom.int - Advice and support on return.
entity4.id10.entry3.title: Integration assistance
entity4.id10.entry3.subtitle: Austrian Integration Fund (ÖIF): German courses, advice, orientation courses for recognized refugees.
entity4.id10.entry4.title: Psychosocial help
entity4.id10.entry4.subtitle: Psychotherapy and psychosocial counseling for trauma or psychological stress caused by the procedure.
entity1.id6.entry5.title: Further steps
entity1.id6.entry5.subtitle: Decisions of the Federal Administrative Court can be appealed to the Administrative Court and/or an appeal to the Constitutional Court.
entity2.id2.entry4.title: Accommodation
